answer:
Your Budget note is now a budget app with the features you listed. It compiles and opens at phone and Mac sizes. I could only preview it with sample data, because previews of your real notes are switched off in Amber Notes settings. So I haven't seen your three months of demo data on screen, and I haven't tried adding, editing or exporting by hand.

- **Month view:** you get spent against budget overall and per category, what's left per day, and a donut chart of spending by category. The arrows move between months, and "Edit budgets" sets each category's budget for that month. The "left per day" figure only counts the days still to come in the current month.
- **Expenses:** the round + button on every screen adds an expense. It has a large amount field, category chips, a date and a note. Tapping an expense edits it, and the edit screen has Delete.
- **Recurring:** rent, subscriptions and the like are added to each month once their day arrives. A recurring expense you delete from one month stays deleted for that month. The new-recurring form's "since" month is today's, so a recurring item you add now fills in from this month on.
- **Search, filter and export:** you can search by note, category or amount, and filter by month and category. CSV exports whatever is currently shown. It downloads a file and also copies the text to the clipboard, in case downloads don't work on the phone.
- **Settings:** currency, the month's start day (1 to 28), and categories. You can add, rename, recolour and delete categories, and set each one's default monthly budget. Deleting a category leaves its expenses as "Uncategorised". There is no confirmation prompt, so a delete takes effect straight away.
- **Demo data:** August to October 2026 with 9 categories, 5 recurring items, and roughly 20 expenses a month. October runs only up to 5 Oct.
